newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds end weaker, underperform U.S. issues.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds end weaker, underperform U.S. issues.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed weaker on Monday, sharply underperforming U.S. Treasuries as weakness in the Canadian dollar and concern about upcoming U.S. data weighed on prices, analysts said.

"It was a weak currency, nervousness about the election (and) a couple of comments out that point to perhaps higher spending. But more generally it's just some fear of the U.S. statistics coming up later this week," said Mark Chandler, a senior economist with Goldman Sachs Canada.
Canada's 30-year benchmark fell C$0.32 to C$107.30 to yield 7.365 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond rose 11/32 to yield 7.11 percent. The spread between the two bonds widened to 26 basis points from 20 basis points at the close of trading on Friday.
Canadian bonds weakened as the Canadian dollar ended softer at C$1.4000 (US$0.7140) on Monday from Friday's close of C$1.3970 (US$0.7158).

Dealers said the currency was unsettled by interest rate speculation and Canadian election jitters. While the dollar shrugged off the start of the federal election on Sunday, it weakened after Prime Minister Jean Chretien said he may reverse some planned spending cuts.

Canadian and U.S. bonds are also looking ahead to this week's key U.S. employment cost, gross domestic product and payroll employment reports. The employment cost index out on Tuesday is the first of the reports, which are seen as a key indication of whether U.S. interest rates will rise further.
In other prices, the Canadian 10-year benchmark bond fell C$0.32 to C$100.98 to yield 6.858 percent. The U.S. bond rose 8/32 to yield 6.91 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds narrowed to 5 basis points from 12 basis points on Friday.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 3.20 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 5.31 percent.
